 According to the Utah Jazz X.com account, Lauri Markkanen suffered a right wrist sprain in Monday’s matchup with the Grizzlies and is considered day-to-day. 
 With Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) out for 6-8 weeks, Utah’s frontcourt rotation is suddenly very thin. Markkanen’s absence should mean more run for Kyle Filipowski, making him a worthwhile waiver wire add. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen (wrist) ruled out vs. Grizzles 
 Markkanen’s wrist looked to bend backwards going through a screen, and shortly afterwards headed to the locker room. This is something worth monitoring over the next few days, with the Jazz’s next game on Wednesday against the Spurs. 
 Jaxson Hayes 
 UTA 
 Center-Forward 
 #11 
 Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) is out for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 After starting Utah’s season opener, Hayes has come off the bench in each of the last two games. His absence could give Josh Okogie and Kyle Filipowski additional rotation minutes, with the latter picking up a DNP-CD on Sunday. Neither is worth streaming. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen amassed 28 points (9-of-19 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers. 
 Markkanen recorded his first 20-point game of the season on Sunday, with the 28 points just six shy of his total in Utah’s first two games. Unfortunately for category-league managers, the Jazz forward recorded no defensive stats, but most roster Markkanen for his offense. Utah begins a three-game Week 2 on Monday against the Grizzlies. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen puts up (6-of-13 FGs), six rebounds, three assists, a steal and four 3-pointers in win on Friday against the Pelicans. 
 The Jazz were able to get into their actions more easily against the Pelicans which allowed Lauri to get more of the shots he wants to take. He was much more rhythm and comfortable in this game. This is the production you expected to have when you drafted Lauri Markkanen in the middle rounds of redraft leagues. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 The Utah Jazz will start Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Ace Bailey, Lauri Markkanen, and Jaren Jackson Jr. against the Pelicans on Friday. 
 Ace Bailey will get the start over Jackson Hayes on Friday. It might be a matchup related change with Murphy, Zion, and Missi being their opponents, but there’s no doubt that Ace was one of the best players on the team on Wednesday. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen in 36 minutes with 18 points (4-of-13 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), 9 rebounds, 3 assists, a block and a three in 123-103 loss to Memphis. 
 Lauri did not have an efficient night tonight, but he got 10 free throws and 9 rebounds. He was a -2 in a 20 point loss. He will be better than he was in this game. Don’t worry about the inefficiency. Lauri will have an opportunity to bounce back on Friday against the Pelicans. 
 Tony Bradley 
 UTA 
 Center-Forward 
 #13 
 Tony Bradley (quad) has been ruled out against the Grizzlies on Wednesday. 
 Bradley will be unavailable for the season opener, which means he won’t be a depth option for the Jazz down low. Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba will play the backup center minutes. 
 Kyle Filipowski 
 UTA 
 Center 
 #2 
 Kyle Filipowski (back) is progressing in his recovery from offseason back surgery but has not been cleared to resume on-court work. 
 Filipowski, who appeared in 77 games last season, missed the final two contests due to a back injury. Ultimately, the 6-foot-11 big man had to undergo surgery to address a herniated disc. According to Jazz head coach Will Hardy, while Filipowski is progressing in his recovery, he has not reached the point where he can resume on-court activities. There’s no concrete timeline, with Hardy simply saying that the Jazz hope to get Filipowski back “soon.” With Jusuf Nurkic (foot) out for at least four weeks, Jaxson Hayes is the most likely replacement at center if Utah sticks with a traditional post player. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen finished Sunday’s win over Denver with a game-high 17 points to go with two rebounds, a steal and three triples across 14 minutes. 
 Markkanen didn’t need much court time to get his buckets, and he led all scorers in the 2026-27 preseason opener. Production has never been a concern for Markkanen, as “The Finnisher” is a strong scorer, rebounder and shooter. Availability is the biggest concern for fantasy managers, but given his first-round upside, Markkanen is shaping up to be a draft-day value in Rounds 3-5.

 Sandro Mamukelashvili tallied 13 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 After totaling 21 points in the Lakers’ first three games, Mamukelashvili has hit double figures in each of his last two. Against the Clippers, his perimeter shot wasn’t falling, as he missed all five three-point attempts. But Mamu was 6-of-10 from two, and he did a little of everything else. Despite the bench role, Mamukelasvhili is worth rostering in deep leagues.

 Quentin Grimes accumulated 23 points (7-of-15 FGs, 9-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and four steals in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 Grimes replaced the injured Luka Dončić (back) in the starting lineup on Wednesday, and he was excellent. He led all scorers with 23 points and added some assists and steals. Grimes shot 0-of-3 from beyond the arc, but he was over 50 percent from two. Even in his usual reserve role, Grimes is worth rostering in deeper leagues because the Lakers need scorers beyond Dončić and Austin Reaves, and he can fill that role. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Kingston Flemings had 23 points (9-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers against the Heat on Wednesday. 
 Flemings came off the bench, played 28 minutes and had the best game of his young career so far. The 19-year-old rookie was impressive with 23 points on 12 attempts from the field and a full stat line. Flemings ended up playing more minutes than starter CJ McCollum, but don’t expect that to continue. Timing Flemings’ next outstanding performance will be difficult given his inconsistent playing time, making him more of a priority in dynasty formats.

 Austin Reaves accounted for 16 points (6-of-16 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 The Lakers didn’t have Luka Dončić (back) on Wednesday, with his absence shifting Reaves into the starting point guard role. Unfortunately for fantasy managers hoping for more production from Reaves, it didn’t happen. More damaging than the field-goal percentage was the turnover count, as he racked up eight. The good news is that the Lakers play two more games in Week 2, starting with the Warriors on Friday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Collin Sexton finished Wednesday’s win over the Clippers with 21 points (6-of-11 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers.
 In his first three games this season, Sexton totaled 27 points on 11-of-28 shooting from the field. With Luka Dončić (back) out, Sexton didn’t move into the starting lineup, but his playmaking role off the bench became even more important on Wednesday. The veteran guard shot over 50 percent from the field overall and 4-of-7 from three in his best performance of the season to date. While he hasn’t been consistent enough to merit a roster spot in 12-team leagues, Sexton is worth considering in deeper leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Trevon Brazile accounted for 11 points (5-of-9 FGs), eight rebounds, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Pelicans.
 After performing well coming off the bench in Denver’s first three games, Brazile made his first NBA start on Wednesday. The rookie forward played 32 minutes against the Pelicans and had another productive outing. The Nuggets needed more athleticism in their rotation, especially after losing Peyton Watson, and Brazile fits the bill. He isn’t a must-roster player in 12-team leagues, but the rookie should be rostered in deeper redraft leagues, even if he doesn’t stick in the starting lineup.

 Ajay Mitchell had 29 points (12-of-20 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Mitchell moved into the starting lineup Monday with the Thunder dealing with a number of injuries and dropped a career-high 30 points in the win over the Suns. He scored 29 points Wednesday against the Mavericks, though it still wasn’t enough to prevent a blowout loss. Nevertheless, Mitchell has become a must-roster player and potentially a league-winner as he continues to produce at a high level when given increased opportunities.

 Cooper Flagg had 26 points (10-of-23 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s 120-96 victory over the Thunder. 
 Flagg is averaging 25.3 points, 6.8 assists, 5.3 rebounds, 2.8 steals and 1.3 blocks through four games this year. The 19-year-old’s game Wednesday against the Thunder was even more impressive considering he also had zero turnovers. Easily the best young player in the league, Flagg may already have elevated himself into being part of the MVP conversation.
